name: Romanovo
summary: Platov's second blow at the Polish cavalry following Bagration. At the crossing of the Moroch at Romanovo, south of Slutsk, a single regiment of Polish chasseurs came on ahead of Latour-Maubourg's corps, misled by a report that made 5,000 Cossacks 500. It beat off three charges in good order before the fourth broke it, and Platov was back across the river, the bridge burning, before the Polish divisions arrived.

sources.label: French & Russian Forces, Battle of Romanov, 14 July 1812 (Nafziger Collection 812GAB)
V. Kharkevich, Platov's actions in the rearguard of Bagration in 1812: the cavalry fights at Mir and Romanovo (1901)

forces.name: Przebendowski's Chasseurs
forces.formation: From Rożniecki's division, IV Reserve Cavalry Corps (Latour-Maubourg)
forces.summary: Sent to seize the crossing of the Moroch at Romanovo, the regiment halted before the village and reported the Cossacks ahead, but its messenger said 500 for 5,000. Platov, seeing how few came on, attacked: three charges were beaten off by carbine fire from squadrons drawn up in echelon, the fourth broke the regiment, and a squadron of the 12th Uhlans and two of Sułkowski's guns checked the pursuit.
notes: Rożniecki's division served in Latour-Maubourg's reserve cavalry corps of the Grande Armée, so it is built from the French list, whose light cavalry brigades take Polish Uhlans; the Grand Duchy of Warsaw's list allows only two regiments a brigade.

About 800 horse: the 1st Polish Chasseurs à Cheval under Colonel Przebendowski, with a squadron of the 12th Uhlans (Small). Nafziger gives the French 1st Chasseurs à Cheval under Colonel Méda, 950 men; the Russian accounts, after Kharkevich, make it the Polish regiment, as here.
Rożniecki's and Kamieński's divisions, with Tyszkiewicz's brigade and a horse battery, came up only after the fight, when Platov had crossed the river and burned the bridge.
A cavalry force on its own has none of the list's Infantry Brigades, which shows as a historical departure. So does its Light Cavalry Brigade without the two Infantry Brigades it needs.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Platov's Rearguard
forces.formation: Rearguard of the 2nd Army of the West (Bagration)
forces.summary: Ordered to hold Romanovo until the next evening so Bagration's baggage could get away to Mozyr, Platov hid four Cossack regiments across the Moroch, then struck the Polish chasseurs when they came on alone. The fourth charge broke them, taking some 350 prisoners, and when Latour-Maubourg's divisions came up Platov was back over the river with the bridge burned.
notes: Platov is the book's named commander.

Nafziger gives Platov's whole rearguard, as here. The Russian accounts put five Cossack regiments, about 2,500 horse, in the fight itself, and send Karpov's two regiments off towards Timkovichi earlier in the day; for the fight, take Kuteinikov's brigade and one more Cossack regiment.
Vasilchikov's regulars and the 5th Jäger held the river line, the Jäger's fire covering the crossing as the Polish divisions came up.
Two Cossack Brigades where the list allows one, and a Jäger Brigade with one regiment where it needs two, show as historical departures.

Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces, except the book's named General of Cavalry Matvei Platov, with his own rating; but 2 of the 4 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.
